reason: Start with the canal sensors to build the head-turning detection pathway.

effect: The completed model connects balance signals to compensating eye movements and posture, alongside vision and information from joints and muscles.
reaction: The opposing eye movement gives the assembled pathway a clear practical purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Integrating the pathways into the body was most worthwhile: the paired head-turning views connect the anatomy to steadier vision and postural adjustment.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the two already-built organs was comparatively uneventful; the picture mainly places them together beside the cochlea.

surprise.text: The weighted-membrane comparison clarified that the organs respond to the start of straight-line motion, not steady motion as such.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the name “otolith organs” appeared without an explanation of the term; the weighted-membrane description made their role clearer.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the sensory structures connected to a familiar reflex made me curious about other integrated functions.
